hedges.reason: This is the most direct instrument for the failure world. A disorderly succession (Putin dying, becoming incapacitated or being removed) is the clearest way the September 2026 Duma vote gets frozen, voided or rescheduled, or the ER label gets overtaken by a new regime vehicle. It also means Russia's leadership changes before 2027.

A Russian state crisis serious enough to postpone a scheduled federal election would take place under martial law, a general mobilisation or regime breakdown. That would threaten Urals exports through the Baltic and Black Sea ports and the pipeline flows, and would bring sanctions whiplash. Front-month crude would take on a supply and risk premium. A postponement decision would have to come around the June 2026 decree window, which lines up with this contract's June horizon.

A Russia-driven security shock (NATO-Russia escalation, nuclear posturing during a succession fight) would send flows into safe havens. Gold would spike above its already elevated range within the same window in which an election-disrupting crisis would take shape.

claims.reason: United Russia can realistically lose the 'most seats' contract only if the election is not held or not certified (resolving to Other) or the regime rebrands under crisis conditions. Both require a Russian emergency that shows up by mid-2026, when the election must be called, and that emergency would disrupt or threaten Russian crude and product exports. Front-month CL would then be pushed well above its ordinary range. A calm oil market and a cancelled Duma election are hard to square.

The regime has treated the Duma election as a routine legitimacy ritual through war and sanctions. Postponing it or displacing ER most plausibly comes from a break in the top leadership, such as Putin's death, incapacity or removal, rather than a choice made under a stable Putin. So a C1 NO world is mainly a world where Putin leaves office in 2026.
